subject.title: fix: stabilize embedded prompt caching across policy and Responses boundaries

question: After the four propagation defects are repaired, should protected `computer`, `cron`, `gateway`, and `nodes` schemas remain model-visible on denied turns with authority enforced only by immutable pre-execution gates?
rationale: This changes where a sensitive boundary is expressed: discovery becomes stable and permissive-looking while actual authority moves to runtime wrappers and MCP grants, which is a deliberate security/product contract rather than a mechanical correctness choice.

options.title: Approve visible schemas with hard denial
options.body: Accept stable schema visibility provided every direct, CLI, MCP, fallback, and reconstructed path preserves immutable pre-hook denial and focused security tests.

options.title: Keep denied schemas hidden
options.body: Reject the cache-stability approach for protected tools and preserve inventory filtering even though it reduces cross-policy prompt-cache reuse.

options.title: Narrow the protected set
options.body: Allow stable visibility only for a maintainer-approved subset and keep higher-risk tools filtered from denied turns.

recommendation.title: Approve visible schemas with hard denial
recommendation.body: Accept stable schema visibility provided every direct, CLI, MCP, fallback, and reconstructed path preserves immutable pre-hook denial and focused security tests.
